Bridging Loan Calculator

The "Cash Out" Tool: If a chain has broken under you, or you're buying at auction, or the property itself is unmortgageable, a standard lender will usually be too slow to help, or will simply say no. Bridging lenders say yes, and they charge a premium for that speed. This calculator shows what the premium really costs.

With most bridging loans you don't make monthly payments. Instead, the whole year's interest is deducted from the loan at the start. Lenders call that arrangement Retained Interest, and it's why the money that reaches you is noticeably less than the amount you've borrowed.
blocks.2:
The Reality Check: Always Have an Exit

A bridging lender cares less about your income than about how the loan ends. You'll need to show exactly how you'll repay within 12 months, perhaps by selling a property or by refinancing onto a buy-to-let mortgage. Lenders call that plan your Exit Strategy, and without a convincing one they won't lend.

The "Default Interest" Trap:
Go even 1 day over your 12-month term and the rate often doubles, from 0.75% to 2.5% a month, say. At that pace the interest tears through your equity, so never take a bridge without a solid Plan B.
